title: NY State Assembly · District 42
area: Ditmas Park, Flatbush, East Flatbush and Midwood, Brooklyn.

context.text: Incumbent Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn and Republican nominee Herman Hall both advanced from their respective primaries, scheduled for June 23, 2026, without appearing on the ballot after the primaries were canceled.

summary.text: Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 42, first elected in 2014. Born in Flatbush, Brooklyn to Haitian immigrant parents, she is the first Haitian-American woman elected to office in New York City. She chairs the Subcommittee on Oversight of Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises (MWBEs) and serves on the Education, Governmental Operations, Health, Higher Education, Housing, and Ways and Means committees.

background.text: Born and raised in Flatbush, Brooklyn, the daughter of Haitian immigrants; is the first Haitian-American woman elected to office in New York City.
Since becoming a legislator in 2015, has introduced more than 200 bills, 34 of which have become law, and co-sponsored more than 250 others, according to her official biography.
Sits on Governor Kathy Hochul's Domestic Violence Advisory Council.

priorities.text: Her official biography lists a focus spanning immigration, education, economic development, unemployment, healthcare access, senior citizen centers, affordable housing, school safety, and women's and LGBTQ rights.

As Chair of the MWBE Subcommittee, has prioritized legislation to help minority- and women-owned businesses, including bills on procurement, contracting notice requirements, and anti-fraud protections.

positions.summary: Sponsored A04991, which would prohibit landlords from using an algorithmic device to set residential rent, and A08454, establishing a tenants' bill of rights.
Cosponsored A1466, the New York Health Act (2025–26 session), which would create a universal single-payer health plan (New York Health) for state residents.

In a January 2019 press release on the Reproductive Health Act, said she voted for the bill, which removes abortion from the state criminal code, because it moves toward women deciding for themselves.
positions.quote: I voted for this bill because I think it is yet another achievement that rightfully swings pendulum back to women deciding for themselves.

positions.summary: In a January 2019 press release on the Legislature's gun-reform package (including court orders barring gun possession by people found to be at risk, a bump-stock ban and a longer waiting period), said she voted in support, adding that the bills do not restrict the Second Amendment.
positions.quote: I vote today in support of the safety and well-being of the people of New York State

record.text: Chairs the Subcommittee on Oversight of Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises (MWBEs); also serves on the Education, Governmental Operations, Health, Higher Education, Housing, and Ways and Means committees in the 2025-2026 session.
Sponsored A04991, prohibiting landlords from using an algorithmic device to determine residential rent; referred to the Housing Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.
Sponsored A08454 (print no. A08454A), creating a tenants' bill of rights; amended and recommitted to the Housing Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A07192, which would prohibit the establishment, incorporation, construction, or capacity increase of for-profit nursing homes; referred to the Health Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A06839, requiring the Division of Housing and Community Renewal to calculate the period of a tenant's rent reduction for diminished services from the date the diminution actually occurred, rather than from a later filing date; amended twice and advanced to third reading as of May 2026.

candidates.name: Herman Hall

summary.text: Herman Hall is the Republican nominee for NY State Assembly District 42, running against incumbent Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn. He advanced from the Republican primary, which was canceled, without appearing on the ballot.

candidates.researchNotes: Hall has a Ballotpedia page (https://ballotpedia.org/Herman_G._Hall) but it carries no biography and he has not completed a Candidate Connection survey. No campaign website or independent news coverage of his background or positions could be found as of this research date.
